The blocking dependence is a genuine value flow, not just an aliased location: `v[jv[i]] = u[ku[i]] * d[i] + c[i]` reads `u[]` after it was just updated (possibly by the very same iteration's `u[ju[i]] += v[kv[i]] * c[i]`, possibly by an earlier iteration). That RAW dependence through the `u` array is what makes DiscoPoP treat the fused loop as unsafe to parallelize, since it can't prove which iterations' writes are visible to which iterations' reads.

The dependence doesn't need to be deleted, only moved: split the single fused loop into two separate loops over the same `i` range —

1. a writing loop that performs every `u[ju[i]] += v[kv[i]] * c[i]` update (each iteration touches only its own `u`/`v`/`c` elements, no cross-iteration accumulation order matters for correctness of the final `u` state),
2. a reading loop that performs every `v[jv[i]] = u[ku[i]] * d[i] + c[i]` using the now-fully-updated `u` array.

Because the first loop fully completes before the second starts, every value the second loop's reads need has already been produced — the same guarantee the original sequential order gave, just re-expressed as "producer loop finishes, then consumer loop runs" instead of interleaved per-iteration. Both loops keep the identical bound `i < LEN_1D`, start value `i = 1`, and `i++` increment, so no bound re-derivation was needed. ## Plan

The fused loop mixes two statements per `i`:
1. `u[ju[i]] += v[kv[i]] * c[i];`
2. `v[jv[i]] = u[ku[i]] * d[i] + c[i];`

Statement 2 reads `u[ku[i]]`, a value that (per the contract's own example of this exact shape) is written by an *earlier* iteration's statement 1, not by anything in the same iteration or a later one — a classic "write now, read later" carried dependence through indirect indices into `u`. Statement 1's read of `v[kv[i]]` is only ever produced by statement 2 of the *same* iteration `i` itself (never by another iteration, since nothing else touches that slot before it's read), so it carries no cross-iteration coupling once statement 1 no longer interleaves with statement 2 of other iterations.

The fix moves the dependence instead of deleting it: split the fused body into two loops over the same range, so **all** of statement 1 (`u` writes) finishes before **any** of statement 2 (`v` writes, reading `u`) begins. Every value statement 2 needs from `u` was produced earlier by the now-completed first loop, so the write-before-read ordering that the original serial execution guaranteed is preserved exactly, just moved from "per-iteration order" to "per-pass order." Neither loop keeps any cross-iteration coupling internally, so each becomes an independent Do-All loop over `i`. Bounds (`1 .. ## Plan

The blocking dependence is the read of `u[ku[i]]` in the second statement, which in the fused loop can see updates from `u[ju[j]] += …` made by *other* iterations `j` (both `j == i` and any `j < i`, via whatever indices `ju`/`ku` produce) — a true flow dependence through the shared array `u` that is carried by the loop, not just reused storage. Because a solution is guaranteed to exist here, the index arrays `ju` and `jv` must each be injective (no two iterations target the same `u`/`v` slot) — otherwise even a sequential rewrite couldn't be made race-free under arbitrary scheduling. Under that injectivity, each iteration's `u[ju[i]] += …` touches a location no other iteration touches, and each iteration's `v[jv[i]] = …` likewise writes a private location, so the only thing standing between this code and two independent Do-All loops is the interleaving that lets the second statement observe a *partial* prefix of `u` updates.

LEN_1D-1`, same bound and increment), so the loop that writes `u` fully completes before the loop that reads `u` begins.
